In 2025, Tokopedia’s buyer experience continued to come under pressure, especially across key areas such as after-sales, customer service, and product quality, where the experience gap versus the key market benchmark further widened. To rebuild buyer trust and restore platform competitiveness, the team launched a dedicated buyer experience improvement project in early 2026, using Ramadan as a key campaign milestone to drive systematic recovery across core experience journeys.

The project focused on two priorities. First, the team strengthened foundational platform capabilities across after-sales, customer service, and product quality. Second, it rebuilt Tokopedia’s differentiated advantages in instant delivery and merchant response efficiency. Teams across after-sales, customer service, product quality governance, logistics experience, seller governance, product, operations, and BPO worked together to improve key mechanisms including cancellation and refund, return SLA, automated review, service capacity planning, DSAT follow-up, product risk identification, instant delivery fulfillment, and merchant response rules.

The project delivered clear experience improvements. In June, Tokopedia’s after-sales NPS moved ahead of the key market benchmark. Q2 human customer service CSAT improved by 9.1 percentage points quarter over quarter, continuing the positive momentum from Q1. TL intervention rate decreased from around 40% to around 15%. During H1, PARR improved by 20%, helping turn the previous NPS gap from behind into a positive lead. On product quality, TLR decreased from 0.45% to 0.30%, while P0-CCR continued to decline and showed a positive long-term trend.

The project also strengthened Tokopedia’s differentiated experience advantages. Instant delivery performance exceeded expectations, with SLA breach completion reaching nearly 2x target and CSAT improving by 15.8 percentage points. Merchant 12-hour IM response rate continued to improve, and Seller IM CSAT was clearly above the relevant internal benchmark. Through this project, the team not only improved key experience metrics, but also rebuilt foundational mechanisms across after-sales governance, customer service quality management, product quality control, instant delivery operations, and merchant response management, laying a stronger foundation for continued buyer experience improvement in the second half of the year.
